passage: Maria: hey roomie! moving in tomorrow, anything I should know? Ganga: hi! yes, quick things so it's not awkward later Ganga: bright white light really gets to me, so I use a small lamp at night Ganga: and strong scents give me headaches, so no room spray if that's ok? Maria: totally fine. I have a lamp too Ganga: also I take the desk by the window, it helps me focus. you can pick the bed side Maria: deal. anything else? Ganga: that's it. I promise I'm not fussy, I just know what makes my week go better Maria: honestly this is helpful. I hate guessing [Two weeks later] Maria: saw you sat near the exit at the orientation talk Ganga: yes, crowds are easier from there Maria: smart. saving you the same seat for the next one

qa.q: Where does Ganga choose to sit at the orientation talk?
qa.a: Near the exit.

qa.q: Why does Ganga explain these needs before moving in?
qa.a: Ganga wants to avoid awkwardness later and seems worried about being seen as fussy.

qa.q: Which approach made the new roommate setup work?
qa.a: Ganga explained the needs briefly and early, and chose the desk and seat that ease the triggers.

qa.q: How does Maria see Ganga's explanation?
qa.a: Maria finds it helpful because Maria hates guessing, and offers to save Ganga's seat.

grounding: It shows a young adult who knows the triggers, chooses seating and routines to ease them and briefly explains these needs as self-care, not fussiness.

passage: The trainee teachers' bus from the block office always filled up by eight, so Gargi came at a quarter to and took the back window seat, where the breeze was steady and no one pressed against her. She wore her soft cotton kurta, never the stiff polyester uniform sari the others preferred. At the school, Irfan, another trainee, found her by the water tank during the loud morning assembly. "Skipping assembly?" "Only the loudspeaker part. It makes my head ring for hours. I told the headmistress; I'm back for the lesson." "She didn't mind?" "She said, 'Fine, as long as your class is ready.' And it always is." Irfan thought about it. "I get headaches from the loudspeaker too. I never thought I could say so." Gargi smiled. "You can. It's not fussiness. It's how I stay good at this."

qa.q: Which seat does Gargi take on the trainee teachers' bus?
qa.a: The back window seat, where the breeze was steady.

qa.q: How does Irfan feel on realising the loudspeaker is a problem for Irfan too?
qa.a: Irfan seems surprised and relieved, realising it is fine to say the loudspeaker causes headaches, which Irfan had never thought possible.

qa.q: Which choices help Gargi stay well at work?
qa.a: Coming early for the window seat, wearing a soft cotton kurta and briefly explaining to the headmistress why she steps out of assembly.

qa.q: How might the headmistress see Gargi's request?
qa.a: She sees it as reasonable, since Gargi's class is always ready.

grounding: It shows a young adult who chooses seating, clothing and routines to ease her triggers and briefly explains her needs as self-care.

passage: In a lecture theatre in Melbourne, Tuan, twenty, always sat at the end of the third row, near the side door. He wore soft, tagless shirts and carried foam earplugs in his pocket. Rosa, new to the course, asked, "Why not sit with us in the middle?" Tuan smiled. "Big crowds and the projector hum wear me out. Here I can focus, and I can step out if I need to." Rosa nodded. "Fair enough." At the café afterwards he chose the table by the window, away from the coffee grinder. They talked about their assignment for an hour. When Rosa went to sit with him the next day, she took the aisle seat without asking.

qa.q: Where did Tuan always sit in the lecture theatre?
qa.a: He sat at the end of the third row, near the side door.

qa.q: How did Tuan seem to feel when explaining his seat to Rosa?
qa.a: He seemed calm and confident, smiling and giving a short, clear reason without apologising.

qa.q: What did Tuan do that showed wise self-care?
qa.a: He chose his seat, clothes and café table to avoid what wears him out, and explained his needs briefly to Rosa.

qa.q: How does Rosa respond to Tuan's explanation?
qa.a: Rosa accepts it easily, saying fair enough and later sitting in the aisle seat beside him without fuss.

grounding: Shows a young adult who knows their triggers, chooses seating, clothing and routines to ease them, and explains briefly, treating accommodation as self-care.

passage: In Room 214 of the engineering hostel, the tube light flickered all evening, and Asif, nineteen, felt his head start to throb within minutes. By October he had worked it out. He switched the tube off and used a warm desk lamp. He kept his headphones on during the loud mess dinner and went for a quiet walk after. He asked his roommate, Suraj, "Can we keep lights off after eleven? Bright light late gives me headaches." Suraj shrugged. "Sure, bro." Other boys joked that Asif was "delicate," but he didn't argue. His grades that term were his best yet, and Suraj started borrowing the lamp too.

qa.q: What did Asif use instead of the flickering tube light?
qa.a: He used a warm desk lamp.

qa.q: How did Asif likely feel when the other boys called him delicate?
qa.a: He seemed secure and calm, not bothering to argue because he knew his choices helped him.

qa.q: Which of Asif's choices were wise responses to his triggers?
qa.a: Switching to a warm lamp, wearing headphones at the loud mess dinner, walking after and briefly explaining his need to Suraj.

qa.q: How does Suraj see Asif's routine by the end?
qa.a: Suraj accepts it easily, agreeing to lights off and even starting to borrow the lamp himself.

grounding: Shows a young adult who learns his triggers, chooses lighting and routines to ease them, and explains briefly, treating it as self-care rather than fussiness.

passage:
Dear Uday,
I'm so happy you're getting married, and I will absolutely be there. I want to tell you my plan now so there's no confusion on the day.
Loud speakers and crowded halls really overwhelm me, so for the sangeet I'll come for the first hour, dance with you, and then slip away. I'll sit near the entrance, not by the DJ.
I'm also wearing a cotton saree instead of the heavy zari one. Heavy fabric makes my skin itch all night.
None of this means I love you less. It just means I'll actually enjoy myself instead of hiding in the bathroom like at Pinky's wedding.
Can't wait to see you as a groom!
Love,
Lakshmi

qa.q: What will Lakshmi wear to the wedding?
qa.a: Lakshmi will wear a cotton saree instead of the heavy zari one.

qa.q: How did Lakshmi feel at Pinky's wedding, based on the letter?
qa.a: Lakshmi felt overwhelmed and uncomfortable, enough to hide in the bathroom.

qa.q: Why is Lakshmi's letter a wise approach?
qa.a: Lakshmi plans ahead, explains needs briefly and kindly, and chooses seating, clothes and timing that make the celebration enjoyable.

qa.q: How might Uday feel reading Lakshmi's plan?
qa.a: Uday may feel reassured and loved, knowing Lakshmi will be there and understanding why Lakshmi might leave the sangeet early.

grounding: Shows a young adult who knows their triggers, chooses seating, clothing and timing to ease them, and explains those needs briefly as self-care.

passage:
Thanks, Uma. So, I'm Karthik, and for years I thought I was just fussy. College lectures gave me headaches, the canteen made me want to run, and I blamed myself.
In second year I started a notes page on my phone. Every time I felt that jittery, trapped feeling, I wrote down where I was. After a month the pattern was obvious: flickering tube lights, scratchy collars, clattering plates.
So I changed small things. I sit near the window now, away from the lights. I wear soft cotton shirts. I eat lunch at eleven-thirty before the rush. In group work I say one line: "Noise hits me hard, so I'll take the quiet corner." People just say okay.
The headaches mostly stopped. Honestly, looking after myself like that isn't fussy. It's how I get to actually be there.

qa.q: What time does Karthik eat lunch now?
qa.a: At eleven-thirty, before the rush.

qa.q: How did Karthik feel before noticing the pattern?
qa.a: Karthik felt jittery and trapped in certain places and put it all down to being fussy.

qa.q: What steps from Karthik's story could help someone with similar triggers?
qa.a: Track where discomfort happens, choose seating, clothes and routines to ease it, and explain the need to others in one short line.

qa.q: How might classmates in Karthik's group see the one-line request?
qa.a: They probably see it as simple and reasonable, which is why they just say okay.

grounding: Karthik learns personal triggers, chooses seating, clothing and routines to ease them, and explains needs briefly, treating accommodation as self-care.
